label: Knowledge Distillation
sub: Teaching smaller models from larger ones
title: Knowledge Distillation
body:
Knowledge distillation is a training technique where a smaller model (the 'student') learns to mimic the behaviour of a larger, more capable model (the 'teacher'). Instead of training the student from scratch on raw data, you train it to match the teacher's outputs — essentially compressing the larger model's knowledge into a more efficient package.

The key insight is that teacher models produce soft probability distributions over possible answers, not just hard predictions. When GPT-4 generates text, it assigns probabilities to every possible next word. These soft targets contain richer information than simple right/wrong labels — they reveal which wrong answers are 'almost right' and capture subtle relationships between concepts. The student learns from this nuanced signal.

Distillation matters because frontier models are expensive to run. A distilled model might achieve 90% of the teacher's quality at 10% of the computational cost, making advanced capabilities accessible for real-world deployment on phones, laptops, or cheaper servers.

sources.label: Hinton et al. — Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network (2015)
